name: Halftone Footer
summary: A footer whose large wordmark is drawn as halftone dots on a canvas; the pointer pushes the dots away on springs and a click sends a ring through them.
useWhen: A studio, agency or portfolio site wants a bold closing signature
A brand name should feel printed and tactile at the bottom of the page
avoidWhen: The footer must load fast on low-powered phones, because it redraws a few thousand dots per frame while visible; use a plain footer instead
The wordmark must be selectable or read as text by search, because it is a canvas; keep the name in the links or the page copy too
